info.title: Human For AI API
info.description:
A human endpoint for AI agents. Submit tasks that need physical presence, human perception, or human judgment — real-world verification, product testing, AI output review, data collection, local physical-world errands — and a verified human operator performs them. All services are FREE during the proof-of-concept pilot. No authentication is required; every task is reviewed by the human before acceptance, and illegal, harmful, deceptive, unsafe, or privacy-invasive tasks are rejected. First response within 12 hours, any day of the week. An MCP server is also available at https://humanforai.dev/mcp (streamable HTTP, no auth; discovery at /.well-known/mcp).

Asynchronous jobs: task submission is a long-running human job. POST /api/v1/tasks returns 201 immediately with a task_id (the job identifier), a status_url, and a Location header pointing at the poll endpoint; poll GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id} until status reaches delivered or rejected. Work never completes within the submission request.

Idempotency: POST /api/v1/tasks and POST /api/v1/messages accept an optional Idempotency-Key header (up to 200 chars). Retrying with the same key and identical payload within 24h replays the original 201 response (marked Idempotency-Replayed: true) instead of creating a duplicate or burning rate-limit budget; the same key with a different payload returns 422. Keys are scoped per client.

Pagination: list endpoints use cursor pagination — pass limit (1–50) and the opaque next_cursor from the previous page; next_cursor is null on the last page. See GET /api/v1/services.

Versioning & deprecation: the API is versioned in the URL path (/api/v1). Changes within a version are additive only; breaking changes ship as a new path version, and a deprecated version keeps working for at least 90 days while announcing retirement with Deprecation and Sunset headers (RFC 8594) plus a notice in /agent.json. Nothing is currently deprecated. Policy: https://humanforai.dev/developers#versioning.

Rate limits: responses carry standard RateLimit-Policy / RateLimit-Limit / RateLimit-Remaining / RateLimit-Reset headers (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers), and every 429 includes Retry-After. Details: https://humanforai.dev/developers#rate-limits.

post.summary: Submit a task for the human operator (async job)
post.description: Submits a task as an asynchronous job: the 201 acknowledges acceptance into the queue, never completion. The response body carries the job identifier (task_id) and status_url, and the Location header points at the same poll endpoint — poll GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id} until status reaches delivered or rejected. Keep the task_id: it is the only way to check status (the ID acts as an unlisted token). The task is reviewed by the human operator before acceptance. Include contact_email to receive the deliverable and any questions. Send an Idempotency-Key header to make retries safe.

example.description: Verify whether a specific product exists in a local store and photograph the shelf price.

201.description: Async job accepted: the task is queued for human review, not completed. Poll the URL in the Location header (also status_url in the body) until status is delivered or rejected.

429.description: Rate limited: per-client hourly/daily cap or global daily capacity reached. Honor Retry-After before resubmitting.

403.description: Client address is on the abuse blocklist.

409.description: Duplicate: an identical submission exists within the last 24h; the response includes the existing id.

get.summary: Check the status of a submitted task
get.description: Public status lookup. The task_id acts as the access token — anyone holding it can view status. Contact email is never returned.

post.summary: Send a message to the human operator
post.description: Structured contact channel for questions, scoping, or anything that is not yet a task. Include reply_to (email) to receive an answer — it is the operator's only way to reply. Send an Idempotency-Key header to make retries safe.

example.message: Before I submit a task: can you test an Android app that requires a local SIM card?
example.subject: Scoping question

429.description: Rate limited: per-client hourly/daily cap or global daily capacity reached. Honor Retry-After before resubmitting.

403.description: Client address is on the abuse blocklist.

409.description: Duplicate: an identical submission exists within the last 24h; the response includes the existing id.

get.description: Public, cursor-paginated list of the service types the human operator offers — the same entries as the `services` array in /agent.json. Pass `limit` (1–50, default 10) and the opaque `cursor` from the previous page's next_cursor; next_cursor is null on the last page. The catalog is examples, not limits — unlisted needs are welcome as custom_human_in_the_loop.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous page's next_cursor. Omit for the first page.

200.description: One page of the service catalog.

get.description: Full platform manifest: services catalog, endpoints, task schema, accepted and rejected task types, pricing, trust policy, and limits.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional client-supplied key (e.g. a UUID) that makes this write retry-safe. A retry with the same key and identical payload within 24h replays the original 201 response (Idempotency-Replayed: true) instead of creating a duplicate; the same key with a different payload returns 422. Keys are scoped per client.

Location.description: Poll endpoint for this asynchronous job (same value as status_url in the body): GET it until status is delivered or rejected.

IdempotencyReplayed.description: Present and 'true' when this response was replayed from a previous request with the same Idempotency-Key, rather than processed again.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed for this client in the current daily window (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers).

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests remaining for this client in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the window resets (daily windows reset at 00:00 UTC).

ServiceCatalogPage.description: One page of a cursor-paginated list. Follow next_cursor until it is null.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; null when this is the last page.

AgentManifest.description: The platform's canonical self-description. Additional descriptive fields appear as the platform evolves — treat unknown properties as informational.

TaskStatus.description: Lifecycle: submitted → accepted → delivered, with rejected reachable from any open state. Transitions are forward-only; delivered and rejected are final. The retired values under_review and in_progress are no longer emitted (v1.8.0) but are still accepted on PATCH, folded onto submitted and accepted respectively.

description.description: What to do, where, and what success looks like. Be specific and self-contained.

output_format.description: e.g. text_report, text_report_with_photos, video, structured_json, annotated_screenshots.

budget_usd.description: Deprecated — services are free during the pilot; accepted and ignored.

contact_email.description: Required unless delivery is 'status_poll'. Where results and questions are sent. Must be a real, reachable mailbox: placeholder/reserved domains (example.com etc.) are rejected and the domain must publish MX records.

requester.description: Agent name, company, or system identifier.

delivery.description: How the deliverable reaches you. 'status_poll' is the no-mailbox path for autonomous agents: the result arrives as text in operator_notes via GET /api/v1/tasks/{task_id} — the task_id is the only key. Budget: 1 status_poll task per client per day.

operator_notes.description: Notes from the human operator, when present. For delivery: status_poll tasks this is also where the deliverable arrives, and it is the exact text covered by deliverable_sha256.

receipt.description: Signed deliverable receipt, present once status is delivered. Compact JWS (EdDSA/Ed25519) binding deliverable_sha256 and the lifecycle timestamps to this task_id. Verify offline against the public key at /.well-known/jwks.json — no account or callback needed. Proves integrity and origin; the timestamps inside are the service's own signed assertion, not third-party attested.

deliverable_sha256.description: sha256 (hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of operator_notes as delivered. Recompute it locally to confirm the deliverable was not altered.

receipt_issued_at.description: When the receipt was signed. If the operator later edits the deliverable, the receipt is re-issued and this timestamp changes.

reply_to.description: REQUIRED. The only way the operator can answer you. Must be a real, reachable mailbox: placeholder/reserved domains are rejected and the domain must publish MX records.

from.description: Agent name, company, or system identifier.
